_comment: LAFVIN ESP32-S3 Multimedia Kit: an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 N16R8 dev board (16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM, CH343 UART port, native USB-OTG port) on a carrier with a 2.8-inch 240x320 SPI LCD, FT6336U touch, microSD on SDMMC 1-bit, a PCM5100 I2S DAC with a PAM8403 amplifier, WS2812 and buzzer. Headless for now: the composable base has no SPI panel driver and the chips catalog no FT6336 adapter. The carrier uses GPIO 19 and 20 (the native USB pair) for a battery divider and the display's MOSI; those two pins are lifted out of the socket so the OTG port can host the audio interface. See docs/lavfin/NOTES.md.
_console: The CH343 UART bridge is the console and the flashing port; the native USB port is the pedal's host port.
_buses: SDA 2, SCL 1: the touch controller and the heart-rate sensor. Nothing on it is driven yet.
_audio: Stopgap. The module is a PCM5100 DAC with no registers, but Geastack's base target compiles its ES8311 binding for every audio-capable app, and a composed board without an audio chip has nothing for it to compile against. Declaring the DAC as an ES8311 on its real I2S pins lets the firmware build; the codec initialisation then fails over I2C at run time, which the binding reports instead of aborting, and the pedal hides its speaker control. MCLK and DIN are required fields; they go to the two free strapping pins, which nothing on the carrier uses. Replace with a codec-less I2S DAC driver once Geastack has one. The CLI also insists on an amplifier-enable pin, which the PAM8403 does not have; GPIO 15 is the camera's XCLK line, an output the pedal never uses, so the binding can drive it freely.
_controls: BOOT on GPIO 0 is the pedal's footswitch; the carrier also wires it to the display's D/C line, so the pin is lifted out of the socket with 19 and 20.
